title: Candy Corn Bag

drivers.name: Price increase (6.0% above regular)
drivers.evidence: Historical week at same price (2026-10-05) sold 3 units (x0.29 vs baseline). Price hikes above 3.85 consistently reduce sales. No past lift observed with price increases. Heatwave not linked to sales rise.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 10.3. No events or promotions are scheduled. The price is 6.0% above regular (3.85), which is a notable increase. Past data shows that 30% off drove a x5.71 lift, but a 10% off only lifted to x1.75. A 6% price increase is unlikely to boost demand. The heatwave (38°C) may slightly increase impulse candy purchases, but no evidence links heat to higher candy corn sales. The recent week with same price (2026-10-05) sold only 3 units (x0.29 vs baseline), suggesting price sensitivity. The noise-adjusted promotion lift is x1.45, but this is irrelevant here—no promotion. No evidence of demand rise from heat. The classical model suggests no effect, which is consistent. Thus, a price increase with no promotion or event suggests a downward adjustment. The baseline is already noisy, so a moderate shrink toward 1.0 is justified.

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-85% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
